unit_result_entry.why_material: With the zero-free parameter specialized to the critical boundary, the proof combines the truncated reciprocal-zeta estimate, the Lindelöf consequence of the Riemann hypothesis, and the unconditional quotient bound to produce an integrable transform-space majorant. Dominated convergence then gives norm convergence of weighted finite natural sums; separate control on the regions below and above one removes the auxiliary spatial weight, placing the limiting function in the closed natural Beurling space.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The entire conditional chain is retained from estimate selection through transform-space convergence, removal of the multiplier, and the membership conclusion.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: The logical chain is stated in prose, but exact decay powers, quotient layout, and the bound at lines 268-271 are formula-sensitive and should be verified from the scan before quantitative reuse.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Fourier-Mellin isometry turns closure into transform-space domination
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The proof changes representation from the original Hilbert space to an isometric Fourier-Mellin transform space. A Mellin identity for the basic Beurling function factors the transform of a weighted finite approximant into a zeta factor and a truncated Möbius Dirichlet sum, so Littlewood's theorem identifies the transformed pointwise limit. This is the structural move that makes analytic estimates usable as norm-convergence evidence.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The unconditional outer limit closes the strengthened criterion
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: After the Riemann hypothesis has supplied natural-space membership for each small positive parameter, the identified transform limit and the hypothesis-free quotient bound give Hilbert convergence as the parameter tends to zero. The previously established pointwise identification fixes the norm limit as the negative characteristic function, and closure then supplies the theorem's nontrivial implication.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The source answers failure of direct natural Möbius partial sums by introducing an analytic weight whose Fourier-Mellin image exposes a reciprocal-zeta Dirichlet approximation; zero-free-region control can then be converted into closure of the natural dilation span.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This is a source-internal proof mechanism, not evidence that every summability scheme or every discrete approximation admits the same analytic bridge; exact displayed formulas require scan verification.

related_synthesis_entries.limit: The synthesis records the proof's direction under the Riemann hypothesis; the reverse implication still relies on the already stated Nyman-Beurling criterion and containment of the natural span in the full span.

after.text:
In essence what has been done is to apply a summability method to the
old natural approximation. The convergence on special subsequences both
of n and of ǫ is also necessary and sufficient, and it is proposed here to study
this alongside with other summability methods for the natural approxima-
tion.
A final remark is in order. Note that we did not employ the dependence
on n in the Balazard-Saias Lemma 2.1. This dependence would seem to be
closely connected to the slowness of approximation to −χ indicated in (1.2).

The proof of Theorem 1.1 provides in turn a new proof, albeit of a stronger
theorem, of the Nyman-Beurling criterion which bypasses the deep and com-
plicated Hardy space techniques. One should extend it to the Lp case, that
is, to the condition that ζ(s) does not vanish in a half-plane ℜ(s) > 1/p. It
should be clear also that we have shown this special equivalence criterion to
be true:
Corollary 3.1. The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the H-convergence
of fǫ,n as n → ∞ for all sufficiently small ǫ > 0.
